reason: Every entry is done, no-effect-yet or cannot-occur. lock.c pick_lock()'s `!IS_DOOR(door->typ)` arm runs in the production game through apply.c doapply(); display.c feel_location() covers its whole reachable-floor branch; dungeon.c update_mapseen_for() and engrave.c engr_can_be_felt() are ported; options.c initoptions_finish() calls reglyph_darkroom(). Five fresh C differentials cover the arm -- a seen wall, lit room floor, the same square under DECgraphics, room floor holding an object, and a blind hero -- and all fifteen segments of scripts/run-apply-lock-pick.mjs match C on every screen, cursor and random-number call. The development standing moved from 1445/7765 screens, 120248/610816 calls, 1471/7765 cursors and 6/33 sessions to 1458/7765, 120419/610816, 1484/7765 and 7/33, with only seed1500-rogue-explore-move changing.

boundary.startingEvent: The hero applies a lock pick, a credit card or a skeleton key and answers doapply()'s direction prompt with an adjacent square whose typ is not a door, so lock.c pick_lock() reaches its `if (!IS_DOOR(door->typ))` arm at 578.
boundary.endingEvent: pick_lock() returns and apply.c doapply():4288 turns that return into ECMD_TIME or ECMD_OK. The observable boundary is the screen that carries "You see no door there." (or its Blind and drawbridge forms) plus whatever the turn that follows draws.
boundary.validInputs: The `a` command with LOCK_PICK, CREDIT_CARD or SKELETON_KEY in inventory, and any getdir() answer naming an adjacent square that holds no monster and no door. Blind and sighted heroes both. The target square may be wall, stone, room floor, corridor, furniture, a drawbridge wall, or floor holding an object or a seen trap.
boundary.observables: The top line, the complete 24x80 screen with attributes, the cursor, the random-number log, loc.remembered_glyph and loc.seenv at the chosen square, svl.lastseentyp at that square and at the hero's own square, engraving erevealed bits, and whether the turn advances.
boundary.exclusions: pick_lock()'s monster and door-mimic arms (560-577), its container branch, its interrupted-attempt resume and the doormask switch's default arm; recalc_mapseen()'s mapseen chain, which writes only mptr->feat.* that this port does not model; feel_location()'s Levitation Rules (777-858), its Underwater return (769-771) and its Punished bc_felt block (865-891); reglyph_darkroom()'s repair loop (1820-1849), which needs a full logical glyph identity and belongs to the open deferral remembered-glyph-caches-a-resolved-presentation.

sourceReview: Complete for the boundary. lock.c 540-593, dungeon.c 2925-2947 and 3075-3200, display.c 270-366, 440-472, 720-905, 940-1105 and 1816-1854, options.c 7335-7350, dbridge.c 137-173, engrave.c 291-313 and engrave.h 44-54 were read line by line against the port. Every branch reachable through the ending event is an entry above; the three feel_location() blocks that stop do so before any write, and the mapseen chain is proved to have no observable effect rather than assumed to. Two known departures from C are recorded in the code: same_remembered_glyph() is coarser than a glyph-number comparison for two objects whose presentations coincide, and reglyph_darkroom()'s repair loop still refuses rather than running, which the ledger tracks as remembered-glyph-caches-a-resolved-presentation.
